text:
Samir: OrionMed (dedicated r-ded-11) reporting P1 — sudden p99 tail jumps and intermittent 503s to /v1/generate starting ~09:12 UTC. CS escalated.
Maya: saw the alert. Initial logs point to a KV cache miss storm and backend GPU queue saturation. Will check routing capacity and pool health.
Lena: metrics: p50 stable, p99 ~2.3s, error rate ~1.7% over last 5m. Spike correlates to a single tenant token sending very long sequences.
Vik: can take a look at serving runtime. Quick question: do we prefer a routing-level workaround or a code-side hotfix first?
Carlos: customer wants an immediate mitigation, even degraded, plus an ETA for a permanent fix.
Priya: I'll keep CS updated. If we can give a 3h ETA for a fix that'd help.
Maya: we can toggle a per-tenant routing override to move OrionMed to r-ded-12 (same region) which has spare capacity. That is low-risk and fast.
Vik: I'll start a hotfix branch addressing queue sizing and a graceful reject path for extreme seq lengths: hotfix/orionmed-backpressure. Aim to open PR in ~40m.
Samir: ownership: Vik = code hotfix, Maya = routing override & revert plan, Lena = metrics/alerts + traces, Priya/Carlos = customer comms. Acknowledge?
Vik: ack. Creating branch and adding tests.
Maya: ack. Applying routing override canary to 10% then ramp. Will post canary result.
Lena: ack. Adding a per-tenant alert (p99>1.5s or error rate>1%). Traces: https://observability.redwood/traces?query=orionmed (cc Vik)
deploy-bot: canary deployment started for routing-override/orionmed -> r-ded-12 (10% -> 100%)
Maya: routing override at 09:18 UTC canary result: error rate down to 0.25% for canary slice. Rolling to 100%.
Carlos: relayed to customer — they confirm noticeable improvement. Asking if this will recur.
Vik: rough ETA: PR open in 40m, review+CI ~1h, canary deploy ~30m. So full ship ~2.5-3h if no blockers.
Priya: told customer 3h ETA for permanent fix and immediate workaround in ~10m. They requested a postmortem.
Samir: good. Maya, can we add a short-term policy to cap max seq length per-tenant to avoid KV storms?
Maya: yes. I'll file a ticket to add auto-routing runbook and a short-term tenant-level seq cap. Will also add a manual toggle to disable KV cache for a tenant if needed.
Lena: collecting traces & logs for postmortem. Annotating timeline: alert 09:12, routing canary 09:18, full route 09:21.
Vik: WIP PR: https://git.internal/redwood/serving/pulls/4721 — queue tuning + graceful reject. Requesting review from Maya & Lena.
Maya: will review in 30m. If green, we'll canary hotfix against backup pool first.
Samir: noted. Priya/Carlos, confirm customer OK with postmortem and give them the incident timeline after ship.
Carlos: confirmed. They want root cause and mitigation plan in the postmortem.
Priya: handling comms, will post a follow-up to the customer success ticket when hotfix ships.
Maya: follow-ups for ops: add runbook step to auto-route on sudden per-tenant p99 spike, add alerting to trigger CS ping automatically.
Lena: also capturing sample payloads (sanitized) to validate the long sequences pattern and include in postmortem.
Vik: once PR is reviewed, I'll coordinate canary with Maya and monitor p99 and error rate. If tests fail, we'll rollback routing change as a fallback.
Samir: thanks all. Keep this thread for updates. If anything regresses, mark urgent and ping #oncall.
